newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases travel rules to boost Pakistan ties.
newsitem.headline: India eases travel rules to boost Pakistan ties.

text.p: India on Thursday announced an easing of restrictions on travel by Pakistanis in what Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral called a "major new unilateral step" ahead of talks between the neighbours next week.
"The measures that I announce today are designed to add to the goodwill between the peoples of the two countries," Gujral told parliament.
"They are an emblem of our earnest desire to establish and maintain relations of friendship and cooperation with our neighbour Pakistan," he said.
India and Pakistan both won freedom from British rule 50 years ago. The two countries have fought three wars since 1947, two of them over the disputed territory of Kashmir.
Gujral praised Islamabad's recent decision to free 38 Indian children detained in Pakistan since 1994 when a fishing vessel on which they were travelling was seized by Pakistani authorities.
The foreign minister said that at present Pakistani nationals could enter India only on visitors' visas designed mainly for trips to meet close relatives.
"In keeping with our policy to promote people-to-people relations, we have decided to permit Pakistani tourists to visit India in groups," he said.
Young and elderly Pakistani visitors will no longer have to report their arrival to police, and visa fees for "senior Pakistanis" will be waived, the new policy states.

Gujral's statement triggered loud protests from the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party which forced an adjournment of the lower house of parliament, demanding the release of Indian soldiers in Pakistani jails.
"There should be no unilateral concessions. Why should there be no reciprocity?" said BJP deputy Pramod Mahajan, just before the Lok Sabha speaker called a 15-minute adjournment.
"We want to know from the government why the proposed visa relaxation the foreign minister has announced cannot be linked with the release of Indian soldiers in Pakistani prisons," Mahajan said.

Talks between the two countries' top diplomats, stalled since January 1994, are scheduled to begin in New Delhi on March 28. Gujral told Reuters on Wednesday he proposed to open up trade with Pakistan.
But he told the upper house of parliament on Thursday that he did not expect "dramatic things" during next week's talks, the Press Trust of India said.
"Both of us will gain by cooperation. I will be more happy if we live as good friends," the news agency quoted him as saying.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda is due to meet his Pakistani counterpart, Nawaz Sharif, on the sidelines of a regional summit in the Maldives in May.
Gujral is scheduled to meet Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub at a meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement in April in New Delhi.
